hints: Focus on what you are really given, a mass of metal and a volume of oxygen gas that react together completely.
Convert that 300 cm3 of O2 at 298 K and 1 atm into moles using pV = nRT, you should get about 0.0123 mol O2.
Link the moles of O2 to moles of metal using the oxide equation (Group 1 needs 4 metal : 1 O2, Group 2 needs 2 metal : 1 O2) and see which metal gives a mass of 1.15 g.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of oxygen used**

We know volume, temperature and pressure of a gas, so we use the ideal gas equation. This is our starting point.

$$pV = nRT$$

**Put in the numbers carefully**

Convert 300 cm3 to m3, use p = 101325 Pa, R = 8.31 and T = 298 K. Watch your units, this is where many students slip.

$$n(\text{O}_2) = \frac{pV}{RT} = \frac{101325 \times 300 \times 10^{-6}}{8.31 \times 298} \approx 0.0123 \text{ mol}$$

**Use oxide stoichiometry to find moles of metal**

The oxide contains $\text{O}^{2-}$ ions, so it is a normal oxide, not a peroxide. For a Group 1 metal M: $4\text{M} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{M}_2\text{O}$. For a Group 2 metal M: $2\text{M} + \text{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO}$.

So moles metal = $4 \times n(\text{O}_2)$ if Group 1, or $2 \times n(\text{O}_2)$ if Group 2.

**Test which metal fits 1.15 g**

If Group 1: moles metal $\approx 4 \times 0.0123 = 0.0492$ mol. Molar mass $= 1.15 / 0.0492 \approx 23.4$ g mol-1. That matches sodium ($A_r \approx 23.0$) beautifully.

If Group 2: moles metal $\approx 2 \times 0.0123 = 0.0246$ mol. Molar mass $= 1.15 / 0.0246 \approx 46.7$ g mol-1. There is no Group 2 metal with that mass (Mg is 24.3, Ca is 40.1). So the metal must be sodium.

options.A: Calcium is Group 2, so 2Ca + O2 -> 2CaO. 0.0123 mol O2 needs 0.0246 mol Ca, which would weigh about 0.0246 x 40.1 = 0.99 g, not 1.15 g. Too light, so it does not fit.
options.B: Magnesium is Group 2, so 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO. 0.0123 mol O2 needs 0.0246 mol Mg, which would weigh about 0.0246 x 24.3 = 0.60 g, only about half of 1.15 g. A common trap if you forget to use pV = nRT and use STP volume instead.
options.C: Potassium is Group 1, so 4K + O2 -> 2K2O. 0.0123 mol O2 needs 0.0492 mol K, which would weigh about 0.0492 x 39.1 = 1.92 g, much heavier than 1.15 g. Correct ratio but wrong Ar.
options.D: Sodium is Group 1, so 4Na + O2 -> 2Na2O. 0.0123 mol O2 needs 0.0492 mol Na, which weighs about 0.0492 x 23.0 = 1.13 g, essentially the given 1.15 g within rounding. This is the only match.
